statements.text: I'm 100 percent behind artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advancing our opportunities for our—for the individuals on the ground.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on U.S. Special Operations Forces resource priorities for FY2024.

statements.text: Today, claims processing tasks, supported by technology to enable automation using artificial intelligence, Natural Language Processing, and Optical Character Recognition, enable automation with data and records extraction from Veterans' electronic health records, verification of military service eligibility, expediting claims that can be decided based on the evidence of record, ordering examinations when required, and the intelligent indexing of the relevant adjudicative information.
statements.context: VA official testimony before the House Veterans' Affairs subcommittees on IT modernization and claims processing automation.

statements.text: Dr. Herman, you mentioned artificial intelligence, strategic advantages, machine learning and how that gives us an operational strategic advantage over our enemies. [...] Does the Hudson Institute—is their stance more in the technological space in order to combat China, Iran, or do you have an opinion on are we losing our footprint with the forces and how does that play out?
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing titled 'Back to the Future,' where Rep. Luttrell questions witnesses about the balance between technological investment and ground-force readiness.

statements.text: It seems like, because industry is very siloed, AI ML is very siloed, depending on the company you work for, as we try to secure artificial intelligence, and we have that human factor, my question is—and this may even sound silly. But, again, I don't know what I don't know. [...] I don't—can AI itself secure AI? Is there any way that we can remove as much error as possible and have artificial intelligence work to secure artificial intelligence? Because as humans, we can't work that fast.
statements.context: House hearing on DHS's and CISA's role in securing artificial intelligence, December 12, 2023.

statements.text: Are you comfortable with the amount of money that you are asking for in the cyber risk, cyber threat domain, and artificial intelligence and machine learning space? [...] there is only $5 million for the new AI office. Are you happy with that number?
statements.context: House Appropriations subcommittee hearing on the FY 2025 DHS budget request, where Congressman Luttrell questions Secretary Mayorkas about AI funding for law enforcement data processing.

statements.text: I think we are really hungry and have a good appetite for the expansiveness of AI in this space. This is where I am going to tell you to be hyperaggressive in order to save these women and children that are in this problem set.
statements.context: House Appropriations / Homeland Security Subcommittee hearing on the FY2025 DHS budget request, where Congressman Luttrell exhorts the Department to deploy AI aggressively.

statements.text: Let me share with you that we are indeed harnessing AI to advance the mission in the fight against on-line child sexual exploitation. At the same time AI presents a risk because the perpetrators use it to advance their depraved criminality.
statements.context: House Appropriations subcommittee hearing on the FY2025 DHS budget request, with Secretary Mayorkas responding to Congressman Luttrell.

statements.text: OK. Are we doing—OK. Well, I am going to make the assumption that since that thing has been handed back to us and globally, that technology and AI, AGI will advance Stuxnet, SolarWinds in some way, and we won't be able to not only keep up, catch up, but I am assuming there is a probability that it is just going to outrun everything. Is that a fair statement?
statements.context: Hearing before a congressional subcommittee on cyber threats to critical infrastructure, marking the 15th anniversary of Stuxnet.

statements.text: Implementation of artificial intelligence, which we do not have the ability to regulate, so the question is who will do that, or do you have the AI system itself regulate itself?
statements.context: House hearing on AI in Veterans Affairs healthcare, with a witness being questioned about data access and AI oversight.

statements.text: we are trying to bring in artificial intelligence to streamline the process. You have 172 different VA facilities, plus satellite campuses, and that is 172 different silos. They do not work together. They do not communicate very well with each other.
statements.context: Congressional hearing on advancing AI in VA healthcare, with the member questioning witnesses about implementation challenges.

statements.text: Where the bad actors, the nefarious actors, are utilizing AI capabilities to hack into the kind-of the sweet spot of what we are not looking at. [...] Mr. Graham, was the—was it a human or software that found the attack or both?
statements.context: Congressional hearing on quantum, AI, and cloud cybersecurity, featuring an exchange between Mr. Luttrell and a witness identified as Mr. Graham.

statements.text: Because I am going to use the term super scientist. This is what AI has created. You have titrated hundreds of attackers down to 2 or 3 that have the capability to ask the AI the question on exactly how to get in— [...]
statements.context: Speaking at a congressional hearing on quantum, AI, and cloud cybersecurity.

statements.text: If we move to a point where artificial intelligence removes the human element, but you needed the human element to find it, what happens?
statements.context: Remarks by Representative Luttrell at a House hearing on quantum, AI, and cloud cybersecurity.

statements.text: I know somebody in your Department who I am going to call as soon as this hearing is over with to ask why implementation of AI and ML is not in this rating discussion, because it makes absolute sense for it to be.
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on VA disability rating modernization, where a lawmaker presses a witness on incorporating AI.
